opening.speaker: winnie
opening.line: If this concerns an assay, say so.

options.text: I'd like to have some soil assayed.
options.say: So would nine hundred men. Get in the book.

options.text: What is it you actually do here?
options.say: I decide what things are. It's the only office in the territory that does.

options.text: I tune pianos.

repeats.say: Mr. Grubb, I have congratulated you twice. There is no third congratulation.

options.text: Do you know a man named Ezra Pike?
options.say: I knew him. Then I certified him. Then I stopped.

options.text: I should go.

options.text: Where do I sign?
options.say: You don't sign. You print. Signatures are for people the next clerk has to believe.

options.text: How long is the wait, honestly?

rephrase.text: How long is the wait now?
rephrase.say: Three weeks. It appears the queue has been on a diet.

options.text: What number am I?

repeats.say: Mr. Grubb, the number does not refresh with enthusiasm.

options.text: I've taken enough of your time. I'll be taking more later.

opening.speaker: winnie
opening.line: You're the piano man with Claim Two.

options.text: I need a certified assay.
options.say: You need to be in a queue that's eight months long and getting longer.

options.text: Eight months? Who's ahead of me?
options.say: The Improvement Company. Perpetually. Priority submissions.

options.text: Has anyone ever brought in Mott gold?
options.say: Ask me that again when you've got something to trade.

options.text: You have very good handwriting.
Would you like to hear about my raccoon?

repeats.say: The answer has not changed and will not change. The raccoon is not an assayable substance.

options.text: I am going to leave now, in a dignified manner.

opening.speaker: winnie

options.text: Will you run my assay?
options.say: I'll run your assay. I'd run your assay if it were a bucket of rain.

options.text: Now can I ask about Mott gold?
options.say: No Mott gold has ever crossed this window. Not one flake. Not in nine years. Not one.

options.text: Has nobody ever noticed?
options.say: I noticed. I wrote it down. I've been writing it down since eighteen and forty-nine, in a book that is not this book.

options.text: Are you all right?
options.say: I am professionally offended, Mr. Grubb. It is the worst kind.

options.text: Thank you. This has been clarifying.

options.text: Run it.
options.beat: She runs it herself, at the window, in front of him — the first assay the player ever watches happen. It is very good gold.

options.text: You knew the nineteen names meant something.
options.say: I knew they meant something. Knowing what is your department. Mine is the book.

options.text: Aren't you going to congratulate me?

repeats.say: I congratulated you about the pianos. Consult your records.
